items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1961-10-13
items.q: David Jones. Mm-hmm. We played out the Suburban Garden. I was playing bass. Played out the Suburban Garden in 1928.

ctx.x: What about this bass with Ridgely when you were with it? Bass with Ridgely? Mm-hmm. Did he have one when you were with it?

Yeah, I'm not sure. Shots was with him a lot. Handy. Sills. David Jones. Mm-hmm. We played out the Suburban Garden. I was playing bass. Played out the Suburban Garden in 1928. Something else I wanted to ask you about.
Did they have many bands that had singers? Oh, no. Uh-huh. They wouldn't hire singers if they were out?

items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1961-02-03
items.q: when I was playing with Ridley, when David Jones would take a solo, the bands would take down.

ctx.x: What was he like before he took out traffic? Was he playing anything else?

No, well, you see, Lewis was a kind of bad boy, you know. See, he first was out of one thing, then another. Used to sell charcoal, had charcoal schooners on the old New Basin Canal. I guess you heard about that. But he was selling charcoal out there, you know. As a kid, you know, see. Well, he wouldn't go to school. And they would pick him up and put him in jail, you know, juvenile delinquency. You know, see. The last time they put Lewis in jail, it kept him in there for indefinite legacy. Well, that's how he…
Did he sing when he was young?
